incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on dedicated pool eu-west-1-ded-42. p99 streaming stalls increased from ~900ms to ~11.8s since 2025-11-02T13:05:00Z. Affected routes: /v1/stream-gen (high qps). Queue depth per shard rising 120 -> 480. Autoscaler reports repeated scale attempts failing with warmup timeouts. Paging oncall.
alex (oncall-sre): I'm paged, picking this up. Setting sev=P1 and starting triage. Who has latest autoscaler logs?
maria (eng-runtime): grabbing logs now. Observed a steady backlog growth starting 13:03Z. Autoscaler hit pool hard limit at 13:06Z and subsequent warmup tasks are timing out. Initial symptoms look like dedicated pool saturation + slow warmup, not a model hang.
maria (eng-runtime): Relevant autoscaler snippet:
```
[2025-11-02T13:06:12Z] scale_request: pool=eu-west-1-ded-42 desired_replicas=8 reason=burst
[2025-11-02T13:06:12Z] scale_response: allowed_replicas=6 (pool_limit)
[2025-11-02T13:07:05Z] warmup_task: pod=ded-42-6 status=timed_out reason=kv-cache-initialization
[2025-11-02T13:07:06Z] request_queue: depth=342
```
jamie (eng-ml): KV-cache coldpath warmup is expensive especially for larger context models. If warmup tasks are timing out, new replicas won't join serving and queue piles up -> tail stalls.
simon (support): We're getting customer tickets: acme-corp reports streaming stalls for live chat, impacts ~12 seats at peak. Beta-inc reports timeouts on embedding endpoints that route to same pool.
kevin (cs): Confirmed — ACME support ticket #AC-9812: "token stream pauses for 8-12s mid-response". They flagged it's affecting SLAs.
alex (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) attempt manual scale (add spare nodes) 2) enable fallback routing for critical customers to hosted path 3) adjust warmup timeout and increase concurrent warmup workers to speed join. I'll coordinate.
ops-bot: Running manual allocation: redwoodctl pools add-nodes --pool eu-west-1-ded-42 --count 2
ops-bot: Command completed: allocated 2 nodes (node ids ded-42-11,ded-42-12). Warmup started.
maria (eng-runtime): Warmup logs show one node failing KV init repeatedly. Suggest increasing warmup timeout to 90s and setting kv-init-retries=5 for this burst. I'm applying a transient config patch: runtime.warmup.timeout=90s runtime.warmup.kv_retries=5
jamie (eng-ml): Also propose toggling model-variant spillover -> route non-critical customers to quantized-small variant to relieve pressure: route policy: spillover=quantized-small if queue_depth>200
rachel (product): We should prioritize customers on enterprise tier and route them to hosted fallback first. Simon, Kevin: please make list of enterprise customers to move.
simon (support): Moving ACME and Beta to hosted fallback now. Support note: informing customers about short diversion.
kevin (cs): ACME on hosted fallback; they confirm degraded-but-functional. Beta on fallback as well.
alex (oncall-sre): After adding nodes and config tweak, p95 dropped from 1.2s->420ms, p99 still at ~3.2s but trending down. Queue depth falling: 412 -> 176.
maria (eng-runtime): Observing one replica repeatedly failing warmup due to nv_cache OOM; we drained that replica. Will patch kernel param for nv_cache GC to avoid OOM next alloc. Also found autoscaler backoff setting was conservative: scale_retry_interval=30s, we'll ramp to 8s temporarily to react faster.
jamie (eng-ml): For long-term: add pre-warm replicas for heavy models, increase KV cache snapshotting to reduce cold init time, and tune autoscaler headroom to avoid hitting hard pool limit.
alex (oncall-sre): Reassigning follow-ups: - maria: implement transient warmup and autoscaler retry adjustments (done in staging, rolling to prod) - jamie: craft pre-warm runbook and quantized spillover rules - rachel: customer communication + SLA impact assessment - simon/kevin: confirm all affected customers on fallback and gather logs for postmortem
simon (support): all affected customers notified; CS incidents created.
ops-bot: Telemetry check: p99 13:05Z=11.8s, 13:15Z=3.2s, 13:30Z=1.1s. Queue depth normalized by 13:28Z.

rachel (product): Please include customer impact table (ACME, Beta) and ETA for permanent mitigations in the postmortem. Also flag potential billing credit for ACME due to SLA.
jamie (eng-ml): Noted. Will start drafting postmortem and include proposed infra changes: pre-warm pool policy, autoscaler headroom heuristics, KV snapshot compression.
maria (eng-runtime): Adding logs and timeline to the incident doc now. Will follow up with exact config diffs for warmup and autoscaler.
